subject: Unexpected 429s — enforcement window mismatch and remediation
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@ajaxhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected 429s — enforcement window mismatch and remediation

Hi Samir,

First, I want to apologize for the disruption your team experienced this morning (approx. 08:55–09:07 PT). We observed an unexpected surge of 429 responses from our tenant enforcement subsystem impacting a subset of requests from Ajax Health. We rolled a targeted rollback at 09:04 PT which restored normal traffic rates; while we are still validating, telemetry indicates request success rates returned to baseline by ~09:07 PT.

What happened (brief): a configuration change deployed earlier today inadvertently widened an enforcement window used by global rate accounting. In combination with Ajax Health’s burst pattern, that mismatch caused token accounting to exceed per-tenant thresholds briefly and trigger synchronous 429s instead of favoring queued/soft-throttle behavior.

Immediate actions taken:
- Rolled back the enforcement-window change (09:04 PT).
- Disabled aggressive synchronous enforcement in the affected layer and enabled graceful queuing for impacted tenants (09:05 PT).
- Applied a short-term tenant-specific override to prevent re-enforcement while we investigate (09:06 PT).

We attached a short incident snapshot and the mitigation patch so your ops team can see what we toggled. We will follow up with a formal postmortem and a remediation plan within 72 hours.

Proposed short-term remediation for Ajax Health (what we can do now):
- Leave the tenant override in place until the permanent fix is live (we will coordinate timing).
- Apply a 1x request replay window to retry a limited set of failed requests if you want us to attempt recoveries (requires confirmation).
- As a gesture for the impact window, we propose a billing credit equivalent to 15% of the tokens billed during the impacted hour; Ben will confirm calculations.

Please let us know: 1) whether you saw any unrecoverable errors on your side (i.e., 429s surfaced to users or blocked critical jobs), and 2) whether you’d like us to attempt request replay for idempotent endpoints.

Again — sincerely sorry for the disruption. I’m on this thread and available if you want to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident_snapshot_20260815.json, mitigation_patch.diff
From: Samir Patel <samir@ajaxhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429s — enforcement window mismatch and remediation

Evelyn — thanks for the quick note and the rollback.

We did see a spike of 429s in our ingest pipeline; roughly 2–3% of calls for that window returned 429 and a small subset (~0.4%) were surfaced to end-users as transient failures (our client retried but a few timed out). We captured a short logs slice and included it here.

Questions:
- Can you confirm whether those 429s were dropped (non-retryable) or if your system queued them and retried? We have some downstream processes that expect at-least-once delivery and the behavior affects reconciliation.
- Appreciative of the credit offer; please send the calculation and we’ll route to billing.

If you think a short call would speed alignment, I’m available 10:00–10:30 PT.

—Samir
Ops Lead, Ajax Health

Attachments referenced: request_sample.log
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@ajaxhealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429s — enforcement window mismatch and remediation

Samir — appreciate the log sample. Quick answers and next steps: 

On dropped vs. queued:
- During the enforcement window breach, the enforcement layer returned synchronous 429s (client-visible). Those responses were not queued at that layer, so upstream retries were required to recover. After rollback we switched the affected layer to queue-and-throttle behavior which preserves in-flight requests for a short period; that change is what allowed most retries to succeed once the surge subsided.

On recoverability:
- We do not have automatic replay of arbitrary customer requests. If you identify idempotent endpoints you want us to backfill, we can run a bounded replay job from our system logs for that tenant (requires a signed consent for replay and a short request id list). If you prefer to handle retries on your end, we’ll keep the tenant override until the permanent fix is live.

Credit calculation (proposed):
- Impact window: 2026-08-15T08:55–09:07 PT.
- Tokens billed during window for Ajax Health: 1,240,312 tokens (per billing snapshot).
- Proposed credit: 15% of billed tokens for the window = equivalent billing credit.

I’ll produce a formal invoice credit note and route to your billing contact once you confirm.

Planned permanent fix (high level):
1) Rework enforcement-window translation logic to ensure tenant burst patterns are evaluated against a per-tenant sliding window rather than the current global window.
2) Add unit + integration tests that simulate high-frequency bursts and gated rollouts for the enforcement flag.
3) Canary the fix with a 24-hour staged rollout and a rollback step.

Neha from Applied ML will run the root-cause analysis and provide timelines for the fix. Neha — can you share an ETA for the dev + canary schedule?

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@ajaxhealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T15:34:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident update: root cause and next steps (Ajax Health)

Hi Samir — follow-up with the more formal post-incident summary and immediate plans. Apologies for the longer note but wanted to be precise.

Executive summary:
- Root cause: a configuration change to the global enforcement-window parameter (intended to tighten short-lived bursts) was translated incorrectly in the tenant accounting layer. Instead of applying a 10s per-tenant sliding window the system applied a global 60s window that aggregated burst counts across tenants during a short period. For tenants with bursty client patterns (Ajax Health), that aggregation caused threshold breaches and returned synchronous 429s.

What we changed (permanent & immediate):
- Permanent fix deployed to staging for review (2026-08-15T12:20 PT).
- Canary rollout started 2026-08-15T14:00 PT to 5% of traffic; monitoring looks good so far.
- Added a guardrail that prevents global translations from rewriting per-tenant windows without an explicit override flag and approval.

Impact and mitigation offered:
- We confirmed ~1,240,312 tokens billed in the impact window. We have applied a billing credit equal to 15% of those tokens to Ajax Health’s account (visible in your billing console within 48 hours).
- Tenant override remains active until full canary completes (expected 2026-08-16T14:00 PT).

Attachments: postmortem_ajaxhealth_20260815.pdf (full timeline, logs, and remediation checklist)

Requested customer action:
- Please confirm whether you’d like Redwood to run a bounded replay for idempotent endpoints. If yes, provide a short list of request IDs or endpoint patterns and a signed consent note.

We’re treating this as a high-priority reliability item. I’ll post the finished postmortem doc and the Jira ticket (HS-34567) with acceptance criteria for the platform team. If you’d like a synchronous call to review the postmortem, Ben and I are available tomorrow.

Thanks for your patience; we’ll keep you updated as the canary completes.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Applied ML — Redwood Inference
